newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Spain praises "dynamic" trade partner Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Spain praises "dynamic" trade partner Argentina.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar on Monday hailed Argentina's transformation into a "modern and dynamic" economy that has made it one of Spain's most important trade partners.

Aznar arrived from Brazil late on Saturday and spent Sunday meeting members of the huge Spanish community and in informal talks with President Carlos Menem. Two days of official business began on Monday with formal talks with Menem.
"Spain and Argentina are two countries with a mature, balanced relationship looking to the future," he said.

Aznar, travelling with 60 Spanish business leaders seeking new opportunities in a country that already buys 15 percent of Spain's exports, spoke of "successes in the economy that have turned Argentina into a dynamic and modern country that has the confidence of world investors."

Spanish firms have spent $1.4 billion on Argentine privatisations, giving them a leading role in the country's telecommunications, air transport, energy and power sectors, besides interests in banking, fishing and food.
The Spanish Chamber of Commerce said 12 top Spanish firms invested more than $7.0 billion in Argentina from 1991-96 and that figure should grow to $11.5 billion by the end of 1999.

Argentina is a member of the Mercosur customs union with Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay -- a trade area with which the European Union signed a landmark pact in December 1995. Aznar said in Brazil that Spain's historic links made it especially well-placed to act as a "bridge" between the two trade zones.
Spain is also firmly behind an initiative for a summit of EU and Latin American leaders in 1998, aired by the French President Jacques Chirac on a recent visit to the region.

Aznar and Menem talked about tensions between Spain and Argentina over a Spanish judge's investigations into the fate of hundreds of Spaniards who were among the tens of thousands who "disappeared" during Argentina's 1976-83 military regime.

Aznar met human rights groups seeking support for Spanish investigators who want the extradition of former military dictator Leopoldo Galtieri and are looking into reports that secret files on the military's "Dirty War" against leftists found their way to Spain.

Argentina put the "Dirty War" leaders on trial in the 1980s and jailed them, but Menem pardoned them in 1989. His government insists they cannot be extradited for crimes for which they have already been tried.

Menem's Chief of Staff Alberto Kohan said the two leaders discussed the "Dirty War" files, but reported that Aznar told Menem "the Spanish government respects every country's laws. They discussed the issue and Aznar ratified that this is a matter in which the Spanish government is not involved."
